title: Medical Superintendent
description: Key Responsibilities1. Clinical Governance & Quality ManagementQuality Assurance: Oversee patient care standards, ensuring high quality, safety, and clinical ethics across all medical and surgical departments.Accreditation & Compliance: Ensure full compliance with medical laws, statutory regulations, and accreditation standards (e.g., NABH, NABL, JCI, BMW management, and local health authorities).Audit & Protocol Oversight: Lead clinical audits, mortality/morbidity reviews, infection control committees, and continuous quality improvement (CQI) initiatives.2. Medical Staff Leadership & AdministrationDoctor Engagement & Credentialing: Manage recruitment, credentialing, privileging, and onboarding of senior consultants, resident doctors, and clinical staff.Duty Roster & Workflows: Oversee duty rosters, call schedules, OPD/IPD coverage, and clinical departmental workflows to ensure 24/7 seamless patient care.Performance & Discipline: Conduct performance appraisals for medical personnel, address clinical grievances, and resolve medical-legal issues or patient disputes.3. Hospital Operations & Strategic PlanningDepartmental Alignment: Coordinate between clinical teams, nursing administration, paramedic departments, and non-clinical operations (SCM, Pharmacy, Front Office).Resource Optimization: Ensure effective utilization of hospital beds, OTs, ICUs, and advanced medical equipment in collaboration with operational leads.Crisis Management: Lead emergency response plans, outbreak responses, and disaster management strategies within the facility.4. Medico-Legal & Regulatory ComplianceLegal Affairs: Act as the primary authority for hospital medico-legal cases (MLCs), clinical consent protocols, and statutory reporting to health authorities.Patient Grievance Resolution: Directly address severe patient complaints, clinical escalation cases, and ethical dilemmas to protect patient rights and hospital reputation.
